mapping.source: Copied pure nativeWrite event-to-record projections; never oracle answers or packet assertions.
mapping.validTime: Fixture ticks map to nonnegative Triplex milliseconds by adding1000000; unbounded beginning sentinel maps0 and end sentinel remains unbounded. Domain fixture cuts are preserved exactly.
mapping.recordedTime: Logical fixture knowledge groups map to deterministic recordedAt=1000+group; each group is one atomic Triplex transact. Native XTDB system time remains independent.
mapping.attributes: Fixture attributes become :w<id>/a<UTF8hex>; generated direct-reference edge facts are charged in the same transaction.
mapping.projection: Put/interval-local patch projections use small fixture write overlays with explicit retract/assert operations. No database or ordinary query is evaluated in the host.
mapping.queries: Independently authored backend-native task queries, typed parameter/result contracts and closed basis relations. No Datalog compilation. Final scalar/result normalization is explicitly charged.
mapping.languageClaim: Multi-query business operations and bounded four-node path witnesses do not establish broad rule composition, query arithmetic, general path counting or incremental maintenance.

limitations: Functional fixture execution only, not scaled comparison, latency qualification, complete schema delegation or all ten goals.
Some business operations use multiple public Datalog queries at the same fixed knowledge cut; normalization cost is included.
Rule closure uses public constrained binary rules over explicitly stored direct-reference edges; additional projected facts are included in write counts.
Schemas are not silently imported from DuckDB's DSL; this runner tests facts/queries and leaves complete Triplex schema acceptance to separate tests.
Five public query surfaces share three Triplex foundations. Native public providers compete; raw probes remain diagnostics and event replay remains the independent oracle.
Upstream44 qualifies the foundation runtime separately; it does not certify arbitrary native queries or every native query-surface feature.
